SATOM 4.13.0

Plugin Studio gets a Code entry (scripts and the apps that depend on them), a Dependencies tab on every app and plugin installs that run as jobs; scripts can write the data stores they declare, which hold 50,000 rows; every plugin reads the fleet's inventory and hardware; the console refuses to start in production without its FERNET_KEY and SECRET_KEY; pages follow the exact build of each FortiWeb.

👤 ForViewerOperatorAdministratorAdvanced user
On this page
  • In short
  • Added

Released: 2026-11-15 · All releases

In short#

Everything in 4.12.0 and earlier applies. A server on 4.12.0 or one of the releases before it that has a delta can take the small delta package (satom-update-4.13.0-from-<its version>.tar.gz) instead of the full one. No database migration runs on this update.

Check one thing before you upgrade a production node: its .env file must set FERNET_KEY and SECRET_KEY, with the same values on both HA nodes. From this release a production node stops at start-up without them (see Security).

Added#

  • Plugin Studio › Code. A new Code entry lists every script with Used by (the apps that run it, linking to their Dependencies tab), From package, status, published version and audience, with Edit, Download and Enable / Disable; Import a script and Developer kit moved there. A script a flow app runs is that app's dependency: no row under Apps or Plugins, in the Apps-only portal or in Operations › Automation › Scripts. A script no app runs stays an app of its own. See Script Library.
  • Every plugin reads the fleet's inventory and hardware, nothing to publish first. The built-in dataset fleet_appliances now carries model, serial, hardware type, HA mode and VIP, last status, zone, department, line, tags and maintenance flag (never a credential), and the new fleet_hardware holds each device's last hardware scan. Both are cut to the person viewing. Fleet Inventory 2.1.0 reads them, so its model, serial, CPU, RAM and classification columns are no longer empty.
  • A script writes a data store it declares; stores and files grow. A script that declares store:<slug> can replace that store's rows: every row is checked first, one commit, and a bad row leaves the old rows. Only declared stores are writable. Data stores hold 50,000 rows / 40 MiB (was 20,000 / 16 MiB). See Data stores.
  • A plugin carries its own code. A script can take a file field, an app form can pass it on with a Run a script step, result() returns up to 8 MiB (was 256 KiB), and a connection call accepts max_mb (up to 64 MiB). An app package upgrades its own script unless someone edited it or another package installed it (then it is kept with a warning). VM Inventory 1.5.0 is the first plugin built this way.
  • Every app lists what it depends on. Plugin Studio › Apps › app has a Dependencies tab: data stores, connections (with whether the secret is set), API Catalog versions, sign-in directories, scripts, apps it opens, automations and the apps that run it, each linking to its page. What stops the app on this server is listed on top and the tab's badge turns amber. See Plugin Studio apps.
  • A plugin upload shows progress, and the install is a job. Import shows a progress bar, then Checking the package…; Install runs as a job with one line per step and opens its progress page if it takes over two seconds. It has no Stop. See Jobs.
  • Runs show what SATOM did and decided. Each step says who did it (SATOM, Person or Instructions), where its answer led, and keeps ping, traceroute and console output under Output. A finished run lists Not run on this path.
  • Web Server Manager: the agent can sign in as an account sshd already lets in. Install and Reinstall ask for the Agent account: satom-mon or the installing credential's account (never root). The installer creates nothing for the latter and keeps its password, shell and keys. Remove never deletes an account the installer did not create. The agent job's error is no longer cut off mid-sentence. See Web Server Manager.

Changed#

  • The API Explorer says why a leaf is unknown (by-parent sub-tables, monitor and log endpoints, objects measured absent), and marks sub-tables of an absent object absent.
  • Build compatibility refuses nonsense and explains itself. One build shows its own coverage; an unknown build is an error naming the known ones (HTTP 400); a field renamed between builds is listed once. See Build compatibility.
  • Fleet objects shows and filters the build: a Build column and a server-side filter, also in search mode and the CSV. See Fleet objects.
  • Config Compare knows the two devices may run different builds. Each line shows both builds; differences the build diff explains are marked, with a build only badge. The verdict does not change. See Config Compare.
  • One answer to "does this build have this page" for the menu, the page, the banner and the build diff. A page whose object the build was measured not to have leaves the menu; its address answers read-only with a sentence and no Create New or Save. A never-measured object stays and says Not measured on this build yet.
  • A page the device shows under two names appears once (Let's Encrypt / ACME, Mobile API, OCSP, Web Anti-Defacement).
  • One sentence says where a layout comes from, everywhere: Layout measured on FortiWeb 8.0.6 build0116 · this device runs 8.0.8 build0140 · same train, with a badge.
  • A dropdown no longer turns into a text box when another build's layout lost its choices. The choices come from the device's own build, then the nearest layout (marked not verified); only with neither is it a text box.
  • Fields the build lacks are marked not on 8.0.8 (with the new name when known) or not measured on 8.0.8. Display only; Save follows the build check.
  • A failed read shows the device's answer: HTTP status, error code and message, and whether the device was unreachable, does not serve the object or refused the read.
  • FortiWeb with ADOMs enabled. A root-ADOM row now says ADOMs are enabled and to register the device again with the ADOM's name, instead of "In use 0 / 50".
  • File fields take up to 20 MiB, and the app run route takes them. The run route refused bodies over 1 MiB, so a 2 MB file never arrived; it now takes a body sized for 20 MiB only for an app whose form has a File field.
  • The app editor names the installed plugin version (package 2.0.1) and shows SATOM's publish counter as #4 published; the Apps list has a Version column, and form, view and Custom Views pages show the version.
  • Plugin Studio shows what Report Studio has: Custom views and Code plugins tables for every ADOM you may enter, only for Report Studio holders.
  • A non-author sees what a runbook check found (HTTPS, TCP, ping, traceroute, login, power state…). Console output and general-step detail stay with authors.
  • Session login works with JSON-only token APIs. A refused form login is retried as JSON, the token is found under common names at the top level or in data / result / response, and a load balancer's cookie no longer drops the bearer.

Security#

  • No real network address in documentation, form hints or tests. The appliance form asks for an IP address or hostname in all five languages.
  • An administrator dataset over the fleet is cut to the person viewing. A dataset whose rows are appliances reached every viewer whole, maintenance devices included; rows are now cut by the appliance's own id.
  • SATOM refuses to start in production without FERNET_KEY. Each process used to invent its own key, so a saved device credential could not be read by another process or after a restart. The web app, scheduler and reconciler now stop at boot with FERNET_KEY is not set; FORTINET_ALLOW_EPHEMERAL_KEY=1 starts a throwaway node. Check that the node's .env has it, identical on both HA nodes.
  • The same rule for SECRET_KEY. Workers signed sessions, CSRF tokens and reset links with different keys: random sign-outs, "expired" forms. Production now stops at boot with SECRET_KEY is not set; FORTINET_ALLOW_EPHEMERAL_SECRET_KEY=1 is its own switch.

Fixed#

  • API Explorer. The CLI evidence statement is decided in one place and shows the selected appliance's own build; "measured" needs a CLI schema and a REST sweep; the page opens on the appliance in ?appliance_id=.
  • Dialogs and forms. Sub-table dialogs are named by their table, never a raw template id; import dialogs (Sign CA, Scanner File Import) are read-only with no Save; Save is offered only over an object that was read and may be written; repeated captions are drawn once.
  • Empty and managed tabs. Firmware and monitor tabs draw one sentence with a link to the Upgrade Flow; a page the build lacks says "not on this build" once; the 150 fully shown objects on the Not in GUI page are one line.
  • Grid sentences wrap instead of clipping at 1440 px and 390 px, and columns bound to nothing read "n/a" with a "not bound" header.
  • One wording for a failed read on every product (FortiADC, FortiGate, FortiAnalyzer, FortiAuthenticator): is unreachable, does not serve this object over REST or refused the read: HTTP 200, Invalid VM License.
  • Renamed objects. The older address redirects to the device's own page with a sentence, and the flash no longer says "OCSP" is called "OCSP".
  • Build compatibility. A page under two names is compared as one; a field the target lacks is reported once; a build whose fields nobody read shows served, fields not measured, never "fits", in the matrix, bindings, list badge and Mass Deploy's Fit column (which now reads fits, adapt, etc.).
  • Fields hidden by an empty ADOM sweep. On an ADOM-enabled FortiWeb 8.0.8 the API Explorer showed "blind, 0 fields" for http_protocol, server_policy and server_pool; it now lists 664 / 245 / 38 fields and templates show their real verdict.
  • More controls, correctly drawn. Selects fed by another collection (SDN Connector, RADIUS Server) are reference selectors; exception dialogs show the keys their layout lacks; the HTTP Protocol Constraints table marks what the build lacks.
  • Caches follow imported knowledge in every process. After a knowledge-pack import, other web workers and the scheduler kept the old overlay, menu and exception index until a restart.
  • Colours. Bootstrap defaults meet 4.5:1 contrast; the Fleet WAF export and about twenty stylesheets and drawings use the theme accent instead of the old orange; dark panels (audit drawer, Switch device picker, baseline viewer, HA node cards) are light; Service Diagram and Network Architecture draw on the light theme and zone labels and chips are coloured correctly.
  • Translations. 129 strings were added to the Spanish, German, French and Italian catalogues, and 142 strings of the migration page, page-plugin screens, converted-restore notes and the Scheduler entry are translated.
  • Scripts and integration hooks start on VMs whose kernel refused the sandbox's /proc (bwrap: Can't mount proc). The runner units no longer cover /proc read-only; the sandbox's isolation is unchanged.
  • A sandbox that does not start says so ("the code never ran: "), and System packages shows installed, not usable with the reason instead of "ok".
  • A script whose connection SATOM cannot hand over still runs. A call to that connection raises a ConnectionError with the reason; a connection that does not exist still refuses the run.
  • Plugin views. Bootstrap loads before the view's scripts, so the DNS Records and Delete dialogs of DNS Lookup open again; Search works again because the frame allows forms (they still cannot leave it).
  • A data-store query no longer stops at 5,000 rows; views, Read a data store and updates or deletes by match see the whole store.
  • A connection's secret box says what to type (password, bearer token, API key, OAuth2 client secret or SSH key, and its user).
  • The Builder can check plugins again. Both Builder endpoints had answered HTTP 500 since the FERNET_KEY change.
  • Web Server Manager: an agent install that sshd still refuses says why. The job asks the server, read-only, for sshd's effective settings, key locations, StrictModes, the SELinux label, account and shell state and sshd's log lines. The installer no longer locks or ages the account it creates, adds its key line instead of replacing authorized_keys, falls back to ECDSA where Ed25519 is refused, and Remove right after an install no longer leaves satom-mon behind.
  • Operations › Incidents bounced to the ADOM home in the FortiADC, FortiAnalyzer, FortiAuthenticator and FortiGate consoles; it now opens and lists that ADOM's incidents.

Documentation and tests were updated alongside these changes, including new Design system, Product rules, Technical requirements and App flow documents.

Upgrading#

No database migration runs on this update. Apply satom-update-4.13.0.tar.gz, or the delta from your version, with Software Update or satom execute update package. Before you do, confirm that FERNET_KEY and SECRET_KEY are set in the node's .env file, identically on both HA nodes; a production node without them now stops at start-up. See Software update and Offline update packages.
